claims_disputed.claim: With the right neuro-symbolic decomposition, lower-cost non-reasoning LLMs generate complex workflow DAGs at production-relevant quality without reasoning models
claims_disputed.reason: The plural claim holds for one of two non-reasoning models; GPT-4.1 does not move (-2.2 pp, n.s.) and fails equivalence until ±12. The one positive case (TOST p=0.007, 90% CI [-2.0, +3.6]) is paired by rule over n=635, but the rules come from seven template families. The paper's own scenario-clustered bootstrap gives ±15-25 pp on marginals, and neither McNemar nor TOST accounts for that clustering. GPT-5.3-chat's monolithic deficit is also a model-specific under-production on the long prompt (§5.1), which limits how far 'non-reasoning LLMs' generalizes.

claims_disputed.claim: Structure does not fix edge-direction (ordering) errors
claims_disputed.reason: The measure is automated keyword coding of the LLM judge's rationales (App. E), with no ground-truth or human check of the category labels. By the paper's own numbers the full Selector+IR system does reduce ordering errors, 12.5 to 9.1 per 100 prompts (about -27%); only Selector->JSON leaves them flat or worse.

missed_issues: Inference ignores the benchmark's clustering. All 635 rules are generated from seven template families, and the paper reports family-clustered bootstrap uncertainty of ±15-25 pp, yet every McNemar and TOST test treats rules as independent. Significance and the equivalence verdict are therefore overstated, and transfer to rule families outside the seven is not estimated.

The review's evidence for the emission-density claim misreads §5.3. For GPT-5.3-chat, monolithic exact-conditions accuracy falls from ~93% at 1-2 pairs to ~0% beyond 15 pairs; the ~55% figure is Selector+IR holding through the 13-15 band. The contrast is larger than the review states.

The 'interpretation is near-saturated' localization is weakest exactly where the effect is largest. GPT-5.3-chat's monolithic node-set accuracy is 82.4% and rises to 92.6% under Selector+IR, so part of its +20.3 pp node-exact gain is node selection, not just emission.

Most of the lift comes from the deterministic compiler, not from adding workflow steps. IR-only (one LLM call plus compiler) captures most of Selector+IR's judge-validity gain on every model (e.g. GPT-5.3-chat +20.8 vs +24.3; Selector+IR minus IR-only is -0.6 to +3.4 pp). The selector mainly buys tokens (0.87x to 0.56x).

Untagged pattern P03 (introduces/mixed): the learned registry selector is vocabulary and exemplar narrowing analogous to a small tool catalog. Selector->JSON vs monolithic is +4.7, +18.9, +4.4 and -3.6 pp, but the paper flags it as not a single-variable ablation.
note: I agree with admit_with_caveats and with the review's P36 'mixed' (the lever is deterministic expansion, not multi-step control flow). I downgrade the general 'non-reasoning LLMs' claim, which holds for one model under rule-level tests that ignore seven-family clustering, and the 'ordering not fixed' claim, which rests on keyword-coded judge rationales and is partly contradicted by 12.5 -> 9.1 under the full system. COI: low on my reading (vendor-affiliated authors, third-party models), the review's medium is also defensible.
